items.title: Implement scripts/fix-sweep.py with sweep and plan-coverage subcommands
items.description:
Create `scripts/fix-sweep.py` as a standalone, Python 3.10+ stdlib-only script with two subcommands. This is the feature's one new code artifact — it exports no Python API and deliberately does NOT import from `scripts/forge-session.py` (it carries its own ~10-line bounded git helper).

Follow the `scripts/validate-traceability.py` / `scripts/check-spec-purity.py` conventions exactly: `#!/usr/bin/env python3` shebang, module docstring with **Usage** and **Exit codes** sections, module-level constants annotated `Final` with `#:` doc comments, `TypedDict` for JSON-boundary shapes (no dataclasses, no Pydantic), Google-style docstrings on every public function, `def main() -> int` + `sys.exit(main())` entry pattern.

Constants to define — the first four are byte-identical to `00-core-definitions.md` §4.3/§5.2; the remainder are per `02-fix-sweep-script.md` §1.3:
- `MIN_NEEDLE_CHARS: Final[int] = 24`
- `VERIFICATION_SEGMENT: Final[str] = ".verification"`
- `DRIFT_GATED_PREFIX: Final[str] = "adapters/"`
- `DRIFT_GATE_SENTINEL: Final[str] = "scripts/build-adapters.py"`
- `VERIFICATION_EXCLUDE_LABEL: Final[str] = ".verification/"`
- `GIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS: Final[int] = 30`
- `GIT_UNAVAILABLE: Final[int] = -1`
- Regex constants: `_NON_ALNUM`, `HUNK_RE`, `H2_RE`, `H3_RE`, `FINDING_RE`, `STEP_RE`, `ADDRESSES_RE`, `FINDING_ID_RE`, `TOTAL_FINDINGS_RE`, `FENCE_RE`

Six TypedDicts: `Needle`, `NormalizedFile`, `SweepHit`, `DroppedNeedles`, `SweepReport`, `PlanCoverageReport` — keys are camelCase at the JSON boundary. One exception class: `UsageError`.

Functions to implement (top-to-bottom order in the file):
1. `normalize(text: str) -> str` — `_NON_ALNUM.sub(" ", text.lower()).strip()`
2. `run_git(args, repo_root) -> tuple[int, str, str]` — bounded subprocess wrapper, never classifies (callers decide skip vs error)
3. `resolve_repo_root(start_dir) -> tuple[Path | None, str | None]` — probes rev-parse --git-dir, --show-toplevel, HEAD; returns (root, None) or (None, reason)
4. `extract_needles(diff_text) -> tuple[list[Needle], dict[str, list[str]]]` — parses `git diff HEAD --unified=0 --no-color` for removed lines + added lines per file
5. `filter_needles(raw, added_by_file, min_chars) -> tuple[list[Needle], DroppedNeedles]` — length floor then reflow/move suppression
6. `list_corpus_paths(repo_root) -> list[str]` — `git ls-files -z --cached --others --exclude-standard`, deduplicated and sorted
7. `applicable_excludes(repo_root, user_excludes) -> list[str]` — always .verification/, conditionally adapters/ when gate sentinel exists, plus --exclude values
8. `is_excluded(path, excludes, user_excludes) -> bool` — segment match for .verification, prefix for adapters/ and user excludes
9. `build_normalized_file(path, content) -> NormalizedFile` — normalize each line into a blob + offset→line map
10. `line_for_offset(nf, offset) -> int` — bisect_right over offsets
11. `dedupe_needles(needles) -> list[Needle]` — one representative per distinct normalized text, first extracted wins
12. `scan_file(nf, original_lines, representatives) -> list[SweepHit]` — one hit per (file, needle), at first match offset
13. `run_sweep(start_dir, user_excludes, min_chars) -> SweepReport` — orchestrates the full pipeline
14. `parse_findings_doc(text) -> PlanCoverageReport` — single-pass state machine over findings headings, fences skipped
15. `run_plan_coverage(doc_path) -> PlanCoverageReport`
16. `render_sweep(report, json_output)` and `render_plan_coverage(report, json_output)`
17. `_build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser` — `sweep` and `plan-coverage` subparsers
18. `main() -> int` — parse, dispatch, map UsageError/OSError to exit 2

CLI: `fix-sweep.py sweep [--repo-root DIR] [--exclude PREFIX]... [--min-chars N] [--json]` and `fix-sweep.py plan-coverage FINDINGS_DOC [--json]`. Exit codes: 0=clean/skipped/not-applicable, 1=findings, 2=usage error. `--json` stores as `json_output`. Reject `--min-chars < 1` and empty `--exclude` as UsageError.

Corpus matching: read each file whole from the working tree, normalize into a blob, `str.find` per needle per file. One hit per (file, needle) at first match offset. Hits sorted by (file, line). Self-file hits count. Files failing UTF-8 or OSError skipped silently, not counted in filesScanned.

Set the executable bit: `chmod +x scripts/fix-sweep.py`.

Do NOT touch any other file — only `scripts/fix-sweep.py` is created in this item.
acceptanceCriteria: scripts/fix-sweep.py exists with executable bit set and #!/usr/bin/env python3 shebang
Module docstring contains Usage and Exit codes sections
Imports are stdlib only — no import of forge-session, no third-party packages
All six TypedDicts (Needle, NormalizedFile, SweepHit, DroppedNeedles, SweepReport, PlanCoverageReport) are defined with camelCase keys
UsageError is the only exception class defined
All module-level constants are annotated Final with #: doc comments
normalize('Universal among the tracked hyperscalers.') == normalize('universal, among   the\ntracked  hyperscalers')
sweep subcommand: exit 0 with skipped=true in a non-repo directory; exit 0 with skipped=true reason=no-head in a fresh git init; exit 1 when survivors found; exit 2 for bare repo or git failure
plan-coverage subcommand: exit 0 when fully covered; exit 1 when uncovered findings named; exit 0 with applicable=false when no plan section; exit 2 for unreadable document
ruff check scripts/fix-sweep.py passes
items.notes: This is the largest item (~350-400 lines of Python). The spec documents are extremely detailed — 02-fix-sweep-script.md contains function signatures, docstrings, and verification checkboxes for every function. Follow them closely. The reflow-suppression filter concatenates added lines per file then delta-wide with single-space joins. The plan-coverage parser must skip lines inside fenced code blocks (FENCE_RE toggling). The diff parser must gate removed/added line recognition on an in-hunk flag to avoid confusing a content line starting with --- for a file header.

items.title: Write tests/test_fix_sweep.py behavior tests (excluding prose guards)
items.description:
Create `tests/test_fix_sweep.py` with pytest + stdlib-only behavior tests for `scripts/fix-sweep.py`. This item covers §2.1–§2.10 of `05-testing-strategy.md`; prose guards (§2.11) are a separate item.

Follow the `tests/test_forge_bootstrap.py` scratch-repo pattern exactly:
- A local `_git(repo: Path, *args: str) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]` wrapper using `subprocess.run(["git", *args], cwd=str(repo), capture_output=True, text=True)`
- `_set_git_identity(repo: Path)` setting `user.email` and `user.name` locally so commits work on CI runners
- Repos created under `tmp_path`

Load the hyphenated module via `importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("fix_sweep", REPO_ROOT / "scripts" / "fix-sweep.py")` in a module-scoped fixture. Unit tests call functions on the loaded module; CLI/exit-code tests run it as a subprocess `[sys.executable, str(SCRIPT), ...]`.

Module constants:
```python
REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
SCRIPT = REPO_ROOT / "scripts" / "fix-sweep.py"
FORGE_FIX_SKILL = REPO_ROOT / "skills" / "forge-fix" / "SKILL.md"
VERIFY_SKILL = REPO_ROOT / "skills" / "forge-verify" / "SKILL.md"
CHECKLISTS = REPO_ROOT / "skills" / "forge-verify" / "references" / "verification-checklists"
```

Test sections to implement:

§2.1 Module foundation: constants exist with canonical values (MIN_NEEDLE_CHARS==24, VERIFICATION_SEGMENT==".verification", DRIFT_GATED_PREFIX=="adapters/", DRIFT_GATE_SENTINEL=="scripts/build-adapters.py", GIT_UNAVAILABLE==-1, GIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS present); UsageError defined.

§2.2 F-5 regression fixture: scratch repo with committed baseline containing the claim in specs/x/PRD.md, verbatim sibling in specs/other/PRD.md, whitespace-reflowed variant in docs/summary.md, un-gated generated copy in src/generated/foo.ts, copy in specs/x/.verification/VERIFY-impl-2026-01-01.md, copy in adapters/claude/skills/x.md with scripts/build-adapters.py as the gate sentinel. Fix = remove the claim from specs/x/PRD.md only. Assert: exit 1, hits for sibling + reflowed + generated with correct file/line/needle/sourceFile/sourceLine, no hits for .verification/ or adapters/, hits sorted by (file, line). Self-file variant: a second copy below in specs/x/PRD.md left unedited → reported.

§2.3 Normalization and threshold units: parametrized over normalize(). Floor: 23 normalized chars dropped, 24 kept. --min-chars overrides.

§2.4 Needle extraction and reflow suppression: hunk-header arithmetic, --- not a needle, reflow suppression (removed line reappearing in added text → no needle), duplicates have distinct provenance.

§2.5 Skip paths: non-repo → reason=not-a-git-repo exit 0; fresh git init no commit → reason=no-head exit 0.

§2.5.1 Git-failure classification: run_git on non-repo returns non-zero (not exception); monkeypatched empty PATH → GIT_UNAVAILABLE and sweep still skip-shapes exit 0; bare repo → exit 2; monkeypatched ls-files failure → exit 2.

§2.6 Corpus boundaries: untracked non-ignored → hit; .gitignored → no hit; conditional adapters/ exclusion; --exclude prefix; --exclude "" → exit 2; binary skip.

§2.7 plan-coverage: 16-findings/15-step → exit 1 uncovered=["V-016"]; total mismatch claimed 16 actual 15; full coverage exit 0; no plan section → applicable=false exit 0; fenced ### V-NNN: not counted; unreadable → exit 2.

§2.8 CLI/output: --json single JSON object, hit-line format regex, verbatim echo.

§2.9 Determinism and read-only: two runs byte-identical; corpus mtimes unchanged.

§2.10 Cost-model shape: monkeypatch counting — ≤5 git calls, one file read per corpus file.

Do NOT add prose guards yet — that is item 008.

plan-coverage tests: 16/15 names V-016, total mismatch, full coverage pass, not-applicable, fenced V-NNN skipped

test_dev_runtime_smoke.py pins impl at 25 checks and the Runnability slice is heading-terminated with .split('\n### ', 1)[0]
test_smoke_command.py pins impl at 25 checks with the same heading-termination

items.notes: The heading-termination fix (D3) is critical — without it, the new CHECK-I24 degradation clauses would contain 'not-applicable' and 'never a hard fail', which are the same literals the existing I21/I22 tests assert, creating a false pass that masks a real removal of those clauses from the Runnability section. The dynamic cross-check test_skill_expected_count_table_matches_the_files re-verifies SKILL totals against the actual files, so a missed edit fails CI twice.

items.title: Add prose guards to tests/test_fix_sweep.py
items.description:
Extend `tests/test_fix_sweep.py` (created in item 002) with prose guards per `05-testing-strategy.md` §2.11. These guards assert that the forge-fix SKILL, checklist files, and forge-verify SKILL contain the exact literals that make the feature's integration load-bearing. Pattern: `tests/test_lifecycle_artifact_check.py`.

The meta-guard contract: the protection set is the enumerated literals below and nothing else.

**Guards over `skills/forge-fix/SKILL.md`:**
- Contains `scripts/fix-sweep.py`, `sweep`, and `--json` inside a bash fence, and `plan-coverage` invoked as `$R/scripts/fix-sweep.py`
- Contains the literal `- Sweep: NOT RUN \u2014 no git delta ({reason})` (em dash U+2014 and `{reason}` placeholder exact)
- Contains all three disposition tokens: `FIXED`, `JUSTIFIED:`, `FALSE-POSITIVE:`
- Contains `git add <path>` and `git add -A` / `git add .` appear only in a prohibitive clause
- Contains `never leave it recorded as` (the failed-FIXED rule)
- Does NOT contain `--exclude` or `--min-chars`
- Step 7's outcome table still holds exactly the seven existing `--outcome` values: `no-findings`, `decisions`, `failed`, `applied`, `reverified`, `reverify-findings`, `deferred`
- Headings `## Step 1:` through `## Step 7:` survive with existing titles
- `## Step 6: Re-verify Gate` through the next `##` heading is **byte-identical** to the pinned pre-change text — store a module constant in the test file captured from the SKILL before the edit
- `references/stage-exit-protocol.md` is untouched and still contains the literal `` `skills/forge-fix/SKILL.md` Step 6``

**Guards over checklist files and `skills/forge-verify/SKILL.md`:**
- `**CHECK-B29**` in backlog.md under `### Work-Order Cardinality` with: `not-applicable`, `never a hard fail`, `` `gap` ``, `by name`, `Report, do not repair`, `(#170)`
- `**CHECK-I24**` and `**CHECK-I25**` in impl.md with their respective degradation/severity literals
- `**CHECK-S39**` in specs.md under `### Internal Consistency` with: `not-applicable`, `` `inconsistency` ``, `` `error` ``, `decision-bearing`, `Report, do not repair`, `(#170)`
- Each new CHECK id appears in its owning dimension-group bullet in the forge-verify SKILL: `(owns CHECK-B29)`, `(owns CHECK-I24/I25)`, `(owns CHECK-S39)`
- `build-adapters.py`'s `RUNTIME_HELPERS` contains `"fix-sweep.py"`

For the Step 6 byte-identity guard: before running the test suite the first time after item 004's edits, capture the `## Step 6: Re-verify Gate` section content from the live SKILL and store it as a module-level constant `STEP_6_PINNED`. The test then asserts that the section extracted from the current file matches this constant exactly.
acceptanceCriteria: tests/test_fix_sweep.py contains prose guards asserting sweep and plan-coverage invocations in forge-fix SKILL.md
NOT-RUN wording guard asserts the exact em-dash literal including {reason} placeholder
Disposition tokens FIXED, JUSTIFIED:, FALSE-POSITIVE: are each guarded
Step 6 Re-verify Gate byte-identity is guarded against a pinned constant
stage-exit-protocol.md citation guard asserts the Step 6 reference is present
Each new CHECK id presence + degradation/severity literals are guarded in their checklist file
Ownership tags (owns CHECK-B29), (owns CHECK-I24/I25), (owns CHECK-S39) guarded in forge-verify SKILL
RUNTIME_HELPERS contains fix-sweep.py guard present
python3 -m pytest tests/test_fix_sweep.py passes
items.notes: The Step 6 byte-identity guard is the strongest C-1 protection — heading survival alone does not detect a body edit inside the Re-verify Gate section. For the outcome-table guard, assert the exact set of seven --outcome values — this detects both additions and removals. The no-cross-reference rule between CHECK-I25 and CHECK-S39 is enforced by the EXISTING test_no_cross_mode_leakage test, NOT by a new guard here.

items.title: Regenerate adapters, add CHANGELOG entry, and run full validation gate
items.description:
This is the closing item — run the single adapter regeneration after all canon edits have landed, add the CHANGELOG entry, and confirm every gate is green.

1. **Regenerate adapters/** by running `python3 scripts/build-adapters.py`. This is run ONCE, after all canon edits (items 003, 004, 005, 006). The regeneration copies `scripts/fix-sweep.py` into every adapter bundle's `scripts/` directory, translates skill prose per adapter, and produces `adapters/*/scripts/fix-sweep.py`.

2. **Verify adapter distribution:** confirm every `adapters/*/scripts/` directory contains `fix-sweep.py` (e.g. `ls adapters/*/scripts/fix-sweep.py`).

3. **Add `[Unreleased]` CHANGELOG entry** to `CHANGELOG.md`. This is a publish-worthy change per AGENTS.md (canon edits regenerate adapters and change what the npm package ships). Add a concise entry under `[Unreleased]` describing: corrected-claim sweep for fix passes (`scripts/fix-sweep.py`), plan-coverage cardinality assertion, four new verification CHECKs (CHECK-B29/I24/I25/S39), forge-fix integration (Steps 2, 4, 5). Reference #170.

4. **Run the full validation gate:**
   - `bash scripts/validate.sh` — includes adapter drift check (step 6b) which must pass after regeneration
   - `ruff check scripts/ eval/` — CI-only gate, run locally
   - `python3 scripts/check-spec-purity.py` — forge-fix ≤300 body lines, forge-verify at 298
   - `python3 -m pytest tests` — full test suite including all new and updated tests

5. **Verify host-neutrality:** `python3 -m pytest tests/test_adapter_host_neutrality.py` must pass — the new checklist prose must contain no host terms in any adapter bundle.

If any gate fails, fix the issue and re-run until all pass.
acceptanceCriteria: python3 scripts/build-adapters.py ran successfully (single regeneration)
Every adapters/*/scripts/ directory contains fix-sweep.py
CHANGELOG.md has an [Unreleased] entry describing the fix-sweep feature (#170)
bash scripts/validate.sh passes (including adapter drift check)
ruff check scripts/ eval/ passes
python3 scripts/check-spec-purity.py passes
python3 -m pytest tests passes (full suite)
python3 -m pytest tests/test_adapter_host_neutrality.py passes
items.notes: The adapters/ regeneration MUST happen after all canon edits — regenerating mid-stream leaves stale content that fails the drift gate. The CHANGELOG entry follows the AGENTS.md publish rule: a canon edit that changes what the npm package ships gets an [Unreleased] entry. The version bump and actual npm publish are owner-gated and out of scope.
